t: Maximum Coins From K Consecutive Bags — Anchored Windows with Prefix Sums
o: We must pick an interval of k integer positions maximizing the total coin value, where coins come in disjoint segments [l, r] each holding c coins per bag. An optimal window's right end can always be shifted so that either its right edge coincides with some segment's r, or its left edge coincides with some segment's l (otherwise you could slide it toward denser ground without loss). So it suffices to evaluate windows ending at p = rᵢ and p = lᵢ + k − 1 for every segment i. For example, with segments [8,10,1],[1,3,2],[5,6,4] and k=4, the window ending at p=6 covers [3,6]: 2 + 0 + 4 + 4 = 10. Since coordinates reach 10⁹ we cannot scan positions — we work segment-wise with prefix sums of full segment values.
k: An optimal window's right end is some rᵢ or its left end is some lᵢ.
Coins in [a,b] decompose into full segments (prefix sums) plus at most two partial edges.
Coordinates up to 10⁹ forbid per-position scans; operate on segments only.

a.n: Approach 1: Anchor Enumeration with Linear Scan
a.i: For each candidate right end p (every rᵢ and every lᵢ + k − 1), sweep all segments and sum their overlap with [p−k+1, p]. This directly expresses the idea and is correct, but costs O(n) per anchor.
s: Sort segments by l (they are given disjoint).
For each anchor p ∈ {rᵢ} ∪ {lᵢ + k − 1}, sum c · overlap(segment, [p−k+1, p]) over all segments.
a.t: O(n²) — 2n anchors, each scanned against all n segments; illustrative only, too slow for n = 10⁵.

a.n: Approach 2: Prefix Sums + Binary Search on Segments
a.i: Precompute prefix sums of each segment's total value. For a window [lo, p], binary-search the first segment reaching lo and the last segment starting at or before p; everything strictly between is counted via prefix sums, and the two boundary segments contribute only their overlapped portions. Evaluating each of the 2n anchors costs O(log n).
s: Sort segments; build prefix sums of c·(r−l+1).
Implement win(p): find first segment with r ≥ lo = p−k+1; add its partial overlap; add full segments via prefix sums up to the last segment with l ≤ p; subtract the last segment's excess beyond p.
Answer = max of win(rᵢ) and win(lᵢ + k − 1) over all segments.
a.t: O(n log n) — sorting dominates; each of the 2n anchor evaluations does two binary searches.
a.sp: O(n) for prefix sums and coordinate arrays.

w: In an interview, state the anchoring argument first (right end at some rᵢ or left end at some lᵢ), then implement the prefix-sum evaluation. Watch for 64-bit overflow: totals can reach 10⁵ segments × 10⁹ length × 10³ coins. Edge cases: k larger than the total span (answer is all coins), a window fully inside one segment, and windows touching segment boundaries exactly. Follow-up: report the actual window positions, or handle overlapping segments (merge them first).
